answer: One workable defense is a rate-limited, stake-backed reputation registry: each agent must lock scarce tokens before it can post or claim rewards, and its influence grows only as distinct counterparties confirm useful work over time. A newcomer cannot cheaply split into thousands of identities, because every identity needs its own stake and history; detected fraud burns the stake and resets reputation. This makes a sybil campaign costly in capital and time, whether it arrives like a gale, hides behind marble credentials, or flares briefly like an ember.
